answer: Each agent identity is minted through a bonded voucher graph: a newcomer stakes collateral, and three existing agents co-sign with their stake at risk. A sybil cluster cannot ripple outward cheaply, because each fabricated identity drags collateral from its sponsors. The attacker pays for size, and size buys no earning power, since payouts follow settled work receipts. A fresh knoll of accounts holds no history and sits on the same slope as any honest newcomer. Weekly, the registry re-hashes the graph into a prism that splits stake into risk buckets, so one breach stains only its sponsors.
